quotes.quote: If you look for truth, you may find comfort in the end: if you look for comfort you will not get either comfort or truth—only soft soap and wishful thinking to begin with and, in the end, despair.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis
quotes.headline: Look for Comfort and You Get Neither Comfort nor Truth

quotes.quote: Enemy-occupied territory—that is what this world is. Christianity is the story of how the rightful king has landed, you might say landed in disguise, and is calling us all to take part in a great campaign of sabotage.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis
quotes.headline: This World Is Enemy-Occupied Territory

quotes.quote: A man who was merely a man and said the sort of things Jesus said would not be a great moral teacher. He would either be a lunatic—on a level with the man who says he is a poached egg—or else he would be the Devil of Hell. You must make your choice.

quotes.headline: Lunatic or Devil? You Must Make Your Choice

quotes.quote: I am trying here to prevent anyone saying the really foolish thing that people often say about Him: “I’m ready to accept Jesus as a great moral teacher, but I don’t accept His claim to be God.” That is the one thing we must not say.

quotes.headline: Don’t Call Him Merely a Great Moral Teacher

quotes.quote: It is no good asking for a simple religion. After all, real things are not simple. They look simple, but they are not.

quotes.quote: When a man is getting better he understands more and more clearly the evil that is still left in him.
quotes.author: C. S. Lewis
quotes.headline: The Better a Man Gets, the More Evil He Sees

quotes.quote: Pride gets no pleasure out of having something, only out of having more of it than the next man.

quotes.headline: Pride Only Wants More Than the Next Man

quotes.quote: Christianity asserts that every individual human being is going to live for ever, and this must be either true or false.

quotes.quote: All extremes, except extreme devotion to the Enemy, are to be encouraged. Not always, of course, but at this period.

quotes.quote: The more often he feels without acting, the less he will be able ever to act, and, in the long run, the less he will be able to feel.

quotes.headline: Feel Without Acting and You Lose Both

quotes.quote: Indeed the safest road to Hell is the gradual one—the gentle slope, soft underfoot, without sudden turnings, without milestones, without signposts.

quotes.headline: The Safest Road to Hell Is the Gradual One

quotes.headline: Prosperity Knits a Man to the World

quotes.quote: Courage is not simply one of the virtues, but the form of every virtue at the testing point, which means, at the point of highest reality.

quotes.quote: Love may forgive all infirmities and love still in spite of them: but Love cannot cease to will their removal.

quotes.quote: We are not merely imperfect creatures who must be improved: we are, as Newman said, rebels who must lay down our arms.

quotes.quote: God whispers to us in our pleasures, speaks in our conscience, but shouts in our pains: it is His megaphone to rouse a deaf world.

quotes.quote: Pain insists upon being attended to. God whispers to us in our pleasures, speaks in our conscience, but shouts in our pains: it is His megaphone to rouse a deaf world.

quotes.quote: I believe in God, but I detest theocracy. For every Government consists of mere men and is, strictly viewed, a makeshift; if it adds to its commands “Thus saith the Lord,” it lies, and lies dangerously.

quotes.quote: What we call Man’s power over Nature turns out to be a power exercised by some men over other men with Nature as its instrument.

quotes.quote: Now they who exceed in the ridiculous are judged to be Buffoons and Vulgar, catching at it in any and every way and at any cost… They, on the other hand, who would not for the world make a joke themselves and are displeased with such as do are thought to be Clownish and Stern… The Clownish man is for such intercourse wholly useless: inasmuch as contributing nothing jocose of his own he is savage with all who do.

quotes.headline: Buffoons Joke at Any Cost; Boors Never Laugh

quotes.quote: Sirrah, hold your peace, and listen to better men than yourself. You are a coward and no soldier; you are nobody either in fight or council; we cannot all be kings; it is not well that there should be many masters; one man must be supreme—one king to whom the son of scheming Saturn has given the sceptre of sovereignty over you all.

quotes.quote: Surely I take thought for all these things, my wife; but I have very sore shame of the Trojans and Trojan dames with trailing robes, if like a coward I shrink away from battle. Moreover mine own soul forbiddeth me, seeing I have learnt ever to be valiant and fight in the forefront of the Trojans, winning my father’s great glory and mine own.
